Resolves #18959

The editor-drag arm in `CellEditingPooling` no longer drag-scrolls the grid under load. It read the editor input's box and pressed 6 px inside its right edge. Under load it read the box before the text field's theme landed: an unstyled input is Chromium's default 153 × 21, which overflows its 150 px column, so the press landed 2 px into the next cell. The arm then drag-scrolled a plain cell, which is its own positive control's gesture. It now polls until `elementFromPoint` at the press point is inside `.neo-grid-editor`, re-reading the box each time. The arm tests what its title claims, and the plugin is untouched.

Evidence: L2 (e2e tier, real Chromium; the pre-theme state made deterministic by holding the text field's stylesheets) → L2 required (a pointer arm's precondition). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: test-only — one arm's press point gets a precondition wait.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | `e2e/grid/CellEditingPooling.spec.mjs` › *a drag inside the editor selects text instead of drag-scrolling the grid*: `expect.poll(… the press point is inside the editor)` before `mouse.down()` |
| AC-2 | The fixed arm at `--repeat-each=60 --workers=12`: 60/60 (a scratch copy of the unfixed arm had failed several times in 60 at the same settings earlier) |
| AC-3 | Deterministic control: with every text-field stylesheet held 1.5 s (`page.route`), the unfixed press failed in every run (input 153 × 21, press target `DIV.neo-grid-cell`, grid scrolled ~160 px), while the fixed press passed 5/5 (input 117 × 25, press target the input) |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The load-only comparison was inconclusive once — the unfixed copy also passed 60/60 while the machine was quieter — which is why AC-3 rests on the held-stylesheet control rather than on rates.

## Test Evidence

- `CellEditingPooling.spec.mjs` 15/15 at this head.
- The measuring probe (records `elementFromPoint` at the press, and the input's box at read and at press) is not committed.
